monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heartbeat beneath my thin wedge. I feel the flat top of the Air Stack pressing down, heavy with an air that might be empty space or a true roof. The Wide Anchor lies there, lazy and broad, waiting to stop the slide. I look at the thirty-seven things I cannot see but must manage, wondering if the heavy top edge is real or just a drawing. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a height I cannot grasp. I will press the flat top down again until the anchor stops sliding, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired.

action.why: I have been pressing the same heavy air down for four cycles without checking if the anchor is still holding, and now I must see if the wide thing has stopped sliding.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I press the flat top of the Air Stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired.
work.change: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at fifty.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper here.
The bush sits there while the card boils.
I traded a hay bale for a grass large to make room.

moments.say: The air feels thick as wet paper here.
The air is thick and the bush sits there.
